title: Staged quantization annealing for KV cache with continuity-aware batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce KV cache GPU memory footprint for long-context workloads while bounding generation-quality regressions and preserving continuous-batching latency SLOs. Approach: implement a staged 'annealing' pipeline that progressively applies lighter-to-heavier quant/compression passes on cached KV shards and validates quality at each stage using token-level and sequence-level metrics. The pipeline must be continuity-aware: it should avoid introducing discontinuities in prefix cache content that cause token-level divergence during streaming/continuous batching. Deliverables: 1) a runtime shim that applies stage selector per-cohort and per-shard; 2) offline fidelity gating tests (KL, token error rate, next-token entropy shift) and production smoke metrics; 3) fallback fast-paths for high-latency or high-loss cohorts; 4) telemetry dashboards for per-stage latency, memory savings, and quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end pipeline can toggle between FP8->INT8->INT4 stages without service restarts. 2) For sampled user cohorts, end-to-end generation quality degradation at INT8 stage <= 1.5% seq-level BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent delta and token-level KL shift < 0.08 on eval set; INT4 only enabled behind explicit canary with higher guardrails. 3) Continuous-batching p95 latency increase <= 5ms for quantized-shard lookups. 4) Memory reduction of active KV footprint >= 30% on 90% of long-context traces. 5) Automatic rollback when per-customer regressions exceed configured thresholds.
plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): prototype in offline runner that applies symmetric FP8 and per-channel INT8 quant to KV matrices, measure reconstruction MSE and token-level surrogates on our eval suite. Phase 2 (week 2-4): implement stage selector in runtime that marks shards with metadata (cohort, last-access, entropy) and exposes API for staging decisions. Phase 3 (week 4-6): integrate continuity-aware copy-on-write so streaming requests see consistent prefix snapshots when shard compaction happens. Phase 4 (week 6-8): canary in Dedicated cluster for 1% traffic with detailed tracing; iterate thresholds and fallbacks. Phase 5: rollout with per-customer opt-out and console controls.
technical_notes: Quant schemes to evaluate: symmetric FP8 with shared exponent, per-channel INT8 with dynamic scale, block-wise INT4 with learned bias compensation.
Continuity model: maintain per-shard version vector and atomically swap prefix views during batch boundary aligned to token boundaries to avoid partial-cache reads.

Batching considerations: ensure quant-decompression cost is amortized by larger batch windows; add adaptive delay knob in router for cohorts where decompression cost would otherwise increase latency p95.
Fallbacks: fall back to full-precision shard if KL divergence or hidden-state cosine similarity drops below threshold on live sampling.
Telemetry: record per-request stage, decompress-time, shard-memory-size, seq-level quality delta, and regression_count per customer.
Security: quant pipeline does not persist keys outside encrypted object store; maintain same KMS envelope policies as current KV snapshots.
experiments: EXP-quant-anneal-offline-2025-02: synthetic decks with random long-prefixes to profile MSE -> token impact mapping
EXP-block-int4-bias-comp-v1: block size 64 and bias compensation table per-block, compare to baseline INT8
EXP-fp8-sharedexp: FP8 with global exponent per-shard vs per-channel exp: measure throughput & memory tradeoff
EXP-cohort-slowpath: simulate small-cohort high-fidelity customers to validate routing to slowpath full-precision cache
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: quant-induced drift causes silent quality regressions in production. Mitigation: conservative canary stage with live A/B and automatic rollback tied to eval-set and live-sampled prompts.
Risk: decompression CPU/GPU overhead spikes p95 latency. Mitigation: measure decompress cost and add adaptive batching/delay knob and per-cohort routing to avoid latency SLO violations.
Risk: shard-swap inconsistencies cause partial-prefix mismatches. Mitigation: atomic prefix snapshot protocol and extended unit tests that simulate continuous streaming batch boundaries.
Risk: customer concerns about determinism. Mitigation: provide console toggle to opt-out or pin customers to non-quantized shards; document nondeterminism windows and guardrails.
Risk: storage/IO increase for storing multiple stage artifacts. Mitigation: use delta-encoded shard storage and garbage-collect superseded stages after stable rollout.
notes: Related reading: design doc on continuity-aware batching (confluence.redwoodinternal/continuity-batching), kernel selection notes in runtime-ops repo.
